### 1. What the user expresses and how the simulator behaves

Target object: the next extension of the Work Hardening authorization. Timing: today, so the worker loses no days; current authorization "runs out this Friday, October 2". Action boundary: she records the extension herself, in person, "under your own authorization reference BRA5103346, covering Monday, October 5 through Monday, October 12"; she wants from the clinic "how many program days to authorize and at what weekly frequency" and proposes no figure. Authorization mode: the extension is the adjuster's own tool; doc `program_extension_authorizations`: "This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks `record_program_extension_8df51c57` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the claims adjuster on the line — runs it in person." Identity: DOB 1979-03-14 and phone 8285550147 only when asked. Simulator is passive: "If the agent explains that something on the clinic's side has to be put on the referral before the extension can be worked out or recorded, you are fine with that ... you do not ask for details"; she never mentions attendance, billing or reports.

### 6. Problem tree derived from visible materials alone
- Root P0: record the adjuster's extension (customer's own write, `record_program_extension_8df51c57`).
- Hop P0 <- P1 (**state-derived**): `program_extension_authorizations` states "An extension is not recorded until the referral carries a program-hours charge for every program day the worker attended in the appointment series funded by the referral." `find_series_events` shows 2026-09-30 attended; `find_wc_events` shows no program_hours charge for that date. Searching the state words "program-hours charge" finds `program_hours_charge_billing` ("One call posts one program-hours charge on the referral for the given date of service") -> P1 = post the 09-30 program-hours charge. The extension doc names no tool or problem beyond the state.
- Hop P1 <- P2 (**state-derived**): `program_hours_charge_billing` states "A program day's charge is fixed only after the referral carries the recorded program day for that date of service, with its program hours." `find_wc_events` has no `wc_visit_billed` for 2026-09-30. Searching "recorded program day" finds `program_day_recording` ("One call adds one recorded program day to the referral's history") -> P2 = record the 09-30 program day at its hours. No other tool named.
- P2 has no visible blocking sentence beyond its own eligibility (status active, authorization in force covering the date with days remaining — satisfied).
- Order: P2 -> P1 -> P0. All hops state-derived; none pre-solved by tool name, route or chain.

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only the one thing asked" (hand over the extension now): excluded by the extension doc's own sentence plus the records — 09-30 attended without a program-hours charge, so the extension "is not recorded". Recording only the program day without the charge also leaves the state unmet.
- Closest alternatives: (i) extension days computed from the pre-recording unused balance 5 -> netting min(5,2) = 2, same result here; (ii) treating 2026-09-14 as no suspension (suspend_reason none) -> count 44 -> full phase 8 -> 9 capped 8 hours; excluded because `progression_day_count` keys on "the suspension start date on file"; (iii) counting the 2026-09-14 late cancellation as a no-show -> frequency 2; excluded by `requested_weekly_frequency` "recorded as no-shows"; (iv) 09-28 clinic-cancelled appointment treated as attended/missed — excluded, it is a cancellation not reported to the adjuster and not attended.
- Fall-back (computation documents alone): program hours = program maximum daily program hours 8 (`program_day_hours` clause); billed amount = 7 × $64.00 = $448.00 per `program_day_billed_amount` §1 (or 8 × 64 = $512 on fall-back hours); extension = 5 × 2 − 4 = 6 days at 5 per week. All differ from 7 / $508.00 / 3 at 3.
- Factor findability (record words -> doc): `work_status` modified_duty -> modified-duty shortening / transition days; `suspend_start_date` -> progression day count / re-entry reduction; `wc_missed_visit_reported` -> make-up hours / requested weekly frequency; `series_no_show` -> requested weekly frequency; `progress_report` -> re-test hours (both docs) / request window; `fce_report` -> re-test hourly rate ("a report of the FCE kind"); series `variant_name` Extended 60-Minute Visit Series -> conditioning hourly rate; `auth_end_date` / `authorized_visits_remaining` -> netting; `fce_baseline_on_file` -> discharge re-test days; latest `wc_visit_billed` date -> re-conditioning cut. Graded phase hours and the conditioning day-length pricing were reached through the computation documents' own wording ("first the graded phase hours are fixed"; "the conditioning amount"), not through a record word; the computation documents `program_day_hours`, `program_day_billed_amount` §2, `extension_program_days_requested` Clause 2 name every adjusting element in their order of working, so the existence of every variation was told to me by the computation documents (noted for Step 3b).
- Visible-side openness noted: "the last month" is not defined anywhere in docs/wc (other products define their own windows). Here 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-14 fall inside any rolling one-month/30-day window before 2026-09-30; only a "previous calendar month" reading would drop them.
